title: The Third Floor
description: At 3:07 AM your elevator stops at a floor that isn't on the panel — your building has no third floor. The doors open onto your hallway, older, and every door stands open except one.

n1.caption: 3:07 AM. Your elevator stops at a floor that isn't on the panel — your building has no third floor. The doors open onto a hallway identical to yours, but the wallpaper is older, and every door is open except one.

n2a.caption: Every open apartment has your furniture — but the photos are wrong. Photos of you at ages you haven't reached. At the end of the hall, one closed door, a brass plate: your apartment number.

n2b.caption: The doors close. The elevator hums up, not down. The display counts floors that don't exist — 4, 5, 6 — and stops at 7. The doors open on a rooftop where dozens of people stand facing the same way. All of them are you.

n3a.caption: Inside is your apartment — but the calendar reads your birthday, next year. On the table sits a contract bearing your signature. The ink is still wet. The pen is still warm.

n3b.caption: The photos span decades — you at 40, 60, 80 — but in every one you stand in this same hallway. The last frame is empty. Written on the back, in your handwriting: 'finally.'

n3c.caption: They all turn in unison. The nearest one — you, decades older — whispers: 'The elevator only comes for one of us at a time. You're the newest.'

n3d.caption: The doors slam and the elevator plummets — you wake in your bed. Morning. Normal. Until the lobby elevator dings, and through the peephole you watch yourself step out.
